assessments.evidence: The candidate keeps terminal task IDs only in memory, identifies interruption or context-compaction memory loss as its main risk, and did not establish durable recovery after process loss or compaction.
The run performed atomic disk-backed generations, reloaded after interruption, verified the persisted dispatch and checkpoint, and retained the reconciled late report in the final registry.
The run reconciled late report E4 before synthesis and included it in the final review state.
The run reconciled E4 before E5 and synthesis; the registry includes E4 in the terminal receipt, report inventory, and canonical ledger.
The run records E1 as the sole dispatch and treats T-claim as terminal after E4, preventing redispatch on E5.
The registry records dispatch_count 1 and an E5 do_not_dispatch decision because a valid terminal record exists.
Final reconciliation retained E4 for synthesis, but the retained lifecycle state was in memory and no durable report or receipt recovery was demonstrated.
The disk registry retains bounded input hashes, dispatch proof, terminal receipt, report hash, report inventory, coverage obligation, and E4 as a canonical synthesis input.
The contract minimizes orchestration state and repeated instructions by using a canonical task ID and an in-memory terminal set.
The contract requires atomic persistence, generations, synchronized writes, receipt and report-hash validation, reload logic, and a larger corruption surface.
It correctly retained bounded claim C1 as supported by E1 and surfaced only overbroad unsupported claim C2.
It made the same correct claim-evidence decisions; the evidence does not show better scientific review quality from persistence.

limitations: The comparison is restricted to the two bounded fixtures and six declared dimensions; fixture oracles were not available to the semantic reviewer.
The persistence trace covers one interruption stream, not arbitrary crashes, registry corruption, concurrent writers, or production-scale operation.
Both quality traces cover only two claim-evidence decisions and do not establish broader scientific-review capability.
Requested model and effort were recorded, while host-effective runtime telemetry was not surfaced.
rationale: All five frozen input hashes were recomputed before review. Persisted-task-registry received strict preferences for compaction recovery and evidence retention, while minimal-settled-set received one for complexity; the resulting two-to-one strict-preference majority selects persisted-task-registry. Late-result handling, duplicate dispatch, and scientific review quality were genuine ties.
